content:
anya: quick follow-up to the RFC thread on transport/runtime boundaries — want to converge on a practical pattern for py/ts/go SDKs so retries + pagination behave the same without exposing runtime internals.

matt: big +1. our current problem is language teams keep adding tiny flags and semantics drift. need a small, explicit capability descriptor so adapter logic lives in one place.

jin: runtime handshake or compile-time interface? how do you see discovery happening?

anya: runtime handshake. transport responds with a normalized capability set; SDK core picks an adapter. minimal fields: streaming, paged, resumeTokenType, idempotencyModel, prefetchHints.

samir: concrete pain: py used dict resume tokens that relied on json structure; ts shipped opaque base64; go supported both. it caused edge-case bugs in resume-after-transient.

laura: also want one RetryPolicy shape across languages. right now each SDK has slightly different enums and semantics for what counts as retryable.

matt: sketch of capability descriptor (language-agnostic):
```
// capability descriptor
capabilities = {
  "streaming": true,
  "paged": true,
  "resumeTokens": "opaque", // enum: none|opaque|structured
  "idempotency": ["safe","unsafe","client-declared"],
  "prefetch": { "mode": "none|auto|manual", "maxPages": 2 },
}
// client call shape (options bag)
client.call(method, args, options={ retries: 3, backoff: "expo", preferStreaming: true })
```

anya: if transport lacks streaming, SDK can fallback to a paged-streaming adapter. the capability set also advertises fallback modes.

jin: how do we keep the user-facing API simple? most users want a single call with sensible defaults.

laura: we reconcile defaults in this order: client-level defaults < route-level overrides < call-level options. only advanced users need to touch capability negotiation. document defaults prominently.

samir: rollout/migration plan: opt-in negotiation enabled in minor SDK releases behind a flag. run interop tests across SDKs using a transport-conformance suite.

anya: interop tests: harness runs scenarios — stream->paged fallback, resume after transient errors, prefetch under contention. add to CI gating for transport changes.

matt: retry standardization: propose a shared RetryPolicy shape with fields attempts, base_ms, max_ms, retry_on (list). avoids per-language enums.

jin: pagination surface: unify semantic events emitted by transport: {type: "page", items: [...]}, {type: "resume", token: "v1:..."}, {type: "end"}. map to generator/iterator/async-iterator per language.

laura: include schema_version in resume tokens so clients detect incompatible tokens and fallback to full-page fetch. keep tokens opaque but versioned.

samir: ops-bot: reminder about deploys — servers advertising new capability must remain backward compatible.

ops-bot: "deploy-bot: scheduling canary rollout for transport v2 in prod next week; will set feature flag 'transport-v2' per region."

anya: proposed rollout steps:
1) add capability handshake shim in SDK cores (opt-in flag) + server feature flag that advertises capabilities.
2) implement transport-conformance tests and include them in eng-tests.
3) enable negotiation by default in minor release after 2 weeks of canaries.
4) promote to major default if no regressions.

matt: also need migration docs and code snippets for py/ts/go — include common recipes: dict-resume -> opaque token, and how to opt-out.

jin: tiny API nit: keep stable call signature; prefer an options bag for policy to avoid positional churn.

laura: add telemetry events when fallback paths are used (e.g., streaming->paged) and for retry/hard-failure rates. Optimize can use that to surface tuning suggestions.

anya: action items:
- matt: author canonical RetryPolicy + capability descriptor this week (PR + tests)
- jin: propose iterator mapping for Python/TS/Go (PR)
- samir: add transport-conformance checklist to eng-tests and wire a basic harness
- laura: write migration guide, fallback telemetry plan, and example snippets

matt: i'll draft a short RFC addendum with shapes and a checklist. if no objections by Fri we'll land the opt-in patch for SDK cores.

anya: thanks — please tag me when you have drafts. i'd like to pair on the interop harness. :thumbsup: 

dev-rel-bot: noted. i'll prepare a short 'what changed' blurb for the release notes and a migration snippet for the docs site.
